guards.what: the offer's pool and filters (TheFutureOfPotions.cs:127): ForNonCombatWithUniformOdds over `Owner.Character.CardPool` with `c.Rarity == targetRarity && c.Type == PotionToCardType[potion]`, WithFlags(NoRarityModification | NoCardPoolModifications), and 3 DISTINCT cards
guards.maps_to: events/the_future_of_potions.py:70-75 filters IRONCLAD_POOL on both clauses and takes `self.rng.sample(candidates, min(3, len(candidates)))`. The pool is right: GetPossibleCards resolves to CardPool.GetUnlockedCards (CardCreationOptions.cs:168-178), which for a non-ascension Ironclad is the whole pool -- the equivalence cards/pool.py:120-133 records. Uniform odds means CreateForReward skips RollForRarity entirely and only strips Basic/Ancient (CardFactory.cs:221-223), which the rarity filter already does. Distinct is right -- CreateForReward accumulates a blacklist and `Except`s it each iteration (CardFactory.cs:91-97, :217) -- and sampling without replacement has the same distribution as the source's sequential Except-then-NextItem. The `min(3, len)` guard matches the source's own inability to fill a short pool. UNLIKE room_full_of_cheese, NoCardPoolModifications IS set here, so the sim's static pool is correct rather than merely currently-unobservable: the four ModifyCardRewardCreationOptions implementers that widen a pool (DingyRug.cs:19, PrismaticGem.cs:34, CharacterCards.cs:46, BigGameHunter.cs:40) all bail on that flag.
